title: Greedy chain-of-thought paths can be inconsistent; self-consistency votes over samples
source_title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
quote: It first samples a diverse set of reasoning paths instead of only taking the greedy one, and then selects the most consistent answer by marginalizing out the sampled reasoning paths.
summary: Foundational paper introducing self-consistency as an alternative to greedy chain-of-thought decoding: sample a diverse set of reasoning paths and pick the answer most paths agree on. It frames inconsistent reasoning paths as the problem that consistency voting addresses.

title: Chain-of-thought rationales may not stay consistent with model predictions
quote: there is little guarantee that the generated rationales are consistent with LM's predictions or faithfully justify the decisions
summary: Distillation study stating that chain-of-thought rationales are not guaranteed to be consistent with a model's predictions or to faithfully justify them, then training a smaller model whose rationales better support its answers.

title: Multi-step math reasoning chains diverge; stepwise self-consistency selects steps
source_title: Stepwise Self-Consistent Mathematical Reasoning with Large Language Models
quote: SSC-CoT employs a strategy of selecting intermediate steps based on the intersection of various reasoning chains.
summary: Reports that complex multi-step mathematical reasoning in LLMs is difficult, partly because potential solutions are explored only narrowly; proposes SSC-CoT, which intersects multiple reasoning chains to select critical intermediate steps, and evaluates step-scored trigonometry problems plus MATH level 5.

title: Small numeric edits to word problems break arithmetic reasoning consistency
source_title: Testing LLM Arithmetic Reasoning Generalization with Automatic Numeric-Remapping Attacks
quote: a model may solve an original problem but fail on structurally similar variants requiring the same reasoning procedure with different numbers
summary: Automatic numeric-remapping attacks that preserve a problem's reasoning program but change small numbers; on GSM8K the tested models lose accuracy on structurally similar variants they previously solved, while shorter, more regular datasets remain stable.

title: Apple reasoning study reports model performance collapsing as complexity rises
source_title: The Illusion of Thinking: Strengths and limitations of reasoning models [pdf]
summary: HN thread on Apple's 'The Illusion of Thinking' paper, which examines strengths and limitations of reasoning models and reports their performance degrading on higher-complexity problems; commenters debate benchmark construction and what the result implies for reasoning claims.

title: Chain-of-thought prompting can reduce accuracy on some task types
source_title: Chain-of-thought can hurt performance on tasks where thinking makes humans worse
summary: HN thread on a study reporting that chain-of-thought prompting can hurt performance on tasks where added deliberation also harms humans; discussion examines when extra reasoning steps help and when they backfire.

title: Mathematician examines which mathematics LLMs actually handle
source_title: What sort of maths are LLMs good at?
summary: Essay examining which kinds of mathematics LLMs handle well and where they break down; the HN discussion contrasts arithmetic failures with textbook-style problems and questions benchmark-based claims of math ability.

title: How LLMs do arithmetic without digit-level computation
source_title: Arithmetic Without Numbers – How LLMs Do Math
summary: Interactive analysis of how LLMs perform arithmetic internally, showing models can reach answers through non-standard strategies rather than digit-by-digit computation; comments discuss why arithmetic behavior is hard to predict from the outside.

title: Long reasoning traces wander between candidate solution paths
source_title: Reasoning LLMs are wandering solution explorers
summary: HN thread on an analysis describing reasoning models as 'wandering solution explorers'; discussion focuses on how they explore and switch between candidate solution paths, and what that implies for consistency and verification.

title: Model misjudges decimal comparison of 9.11 and 9.9
source_title: Can the New Mathstral LLM Accurately Compare 9.11 and 9.9?
summary: Article testing a small math-tuned LLM on the numeric comparison 9.11 versus 9.9, a recurring arithmetic edge case where models misjudge decimal magnitude; the thread debates whether this reflects tokenization artifacts or weak numeric reasoning.
